curation.lead:
Jeffrey A. Schantz (born 1957, BS SUNY Albany 1979, JD Fordham University School of Law 1983, NY Bar 1984) served as Jeffrey Epstein's original senior in-house attorney and fiduciary from May 1995 until approximately mid-2003, predating and initially outranking Darren Indyke in Epstein's legal hierarchy. Both Schantz and Indyke came to Epstein through Gold and Wachtel, a now-defunct boutique New York law firm that represented Epstein from at least 1988. By April 1996, Schantz was acting as Epstein's "transaction counsel" in a State Department property dispute (EFTA01325008) and had been granted power of attorney over 11 East 71st Street via an ACRIS-recorded instrument. A November 1996 flight log places him on an Epstein flight from Palm Beach to Teterboro alongside Epstein, family members, and a minor (EFTA00008920). Martindale.com's legal directory subsequently listed his professional affiliation not as an independent law firm but as "J. Epstein & Co., Inc." — Epstein's personal company — with practice areas in international law, corporate law, tax law, securities law, and litigation.

Schantz held the most concentrated fiduciary power of any individual in Epstein's documented estate architecture. Under the November 8, 2001 trust instruments, he served as co-Trustee of both Trust One and Trust Two alongside Epstein, with singular authority to appoint and remove all successor trustees and executors — Indyke was his designated backup (EFTA01266298, EFTA01266334). He was co-Executor of Epstein's original will with Paul Hoffman. Trust One provided him a $10 million bequest, equal to Epstein's brother Mark. He served as Vice President, Secretary, and Treasurer of the J. Epstein Virgin Islands Foundation and was the only authorized signatory besides Epstein on FirstBank Puerto Rico accounts (EFTA01273238). An October 2003 JPMorgan statement shows NYSG LLC disbursing $500,000 to Schantz versus $200,000 to Indyke, a 2.5-to-1 compensation ratio reflecting his seniority (EFTA01514000). Trust Two, which he co-administered, named Kelly Bovino — later accused by Virginia Giuffre of procurement and sexual abuse — as its sole beneficiary at 100%.

Schantz's departure occurred circa mid-2003. The First Codicil to Epstein's will (June 2003) replaced Schantz and Hoffman as Executors with Henry Jarecki and James Cayne. A contemporaneous trust amendment removed Schantz as co-Trustee, replacing him with Ghislaine Maxwell and Ira Zicherman — he was the only person whose removal required two successors. The Second Amendment to Trust One (December 2004) formally deleted his $10 million bequest (EFTA01266322). In a December 2016 email, when Mark Epstein asked Jeffrey whether Schantz still worked for him, Epstein replied: "Left 13 years ago" and "No bad guy" (EFTA02666903). Despite this departure, an August 2019 SDNY prosecutor email still identified Schantz alongside Indyke as the "likeliest individuals" who "would (or would potentially be able to) send money on his behalf" (EFTA00018951). As of 2026, Schantz maintains zero personal corporate registrations, zero federal court cases as a named party, zero SEC filings, and zero FARA registrations across all searched databases — an extraordinary degree of legal invisibility for someone who held this level of fiduciary authority over tens of millions of dollars.
open_questions: What were the circumstances of Schantz's departure in mid-2003 -- was it related to the Citibank litigation, the emerging criminal exposure from Palm Beach, or an internal dispute -- and did he receive compensation beyond the documented $500,000 NYSG disbursement?

What was Schantz's knowledge of and role in Trust Two's designation of Kelly Bovino as sole beneficiary, given that Bovino was later identified as an alleged procurer and abuser in Epstein's trafficking operation?

Did Schantz maintain any undocumented relationship with Epstein or Epstein entities after his formal 2003 departure, and does the SDNY's 2019 identification of him as a potential financial conduit reflect information not yet publicly available?

What is the significance of the 2006-2007 lobbying registration for 'Jeff Schantz' with JGW International on defense and homeland security issues -- is this the same individual, and if so, does it represent a post-Epstein career trajectory?
Why did Schantz's removal require replacement by two successors (Maxwell and Zicherman) when no other trustee change in the Epstein estate required such redundancy?
curation.system_role: Schantz reveals the architecture of Epstein's original fiduciary control structure: a single in-house attorney who held simultaneous power over trusts, wills, bank accounts, corporate entities, and operational logistics — then vanished from the record with near-total legal invisibility, demonstrating how a purpose-built enabler can be cleanly excised from a network while the network itself continues to function.

sections.title: Origins at Gold and Wachtel
sections.content:
Jeffrey A. Schantz graduated from SUNY Albany in 1979 and Fordham University School of Law in 1983, gaining admission to the New York Bar in 1984. He entered Epstein's orbit through Gold and Wachtel, a boutique Manhattan law firm that represented Epstein from at least 1988 according to a Yahoo Finance investigation. Both Schantz and Darren Indyke came from this firm, establishing a pipeline that would supply Epstein with his two most important legal operatives. Schantz stated he began working with Epstein in May 1995, and by April 1996 he was signing correspondence as "Jeffrey A. Schantz, J. Epstein & Company, Inc." in State Department letters — not as a partner at an independent firm, but as embedded counsel operating under Epstein's corporate identity.

The earliest documented evidence of Schantz's operational role is the April 19, 1996 telephone conference with Richard Massey of the Office of Foreign Missions, conducted in his capacity as Epstein's "transaction counsel" during a dispute over a lease at 401 Broadway (case 96-cv-8307 SDNY, later reported at 27 F.Supp.2d 404). Seven days later, on April 26, 1996, ACRIS records show a power of attorney instrument recorded on 11 East 71st Street, with Epstein and the 11 East 71st Trust as grantors and Schantz as grantee (FT_1490005138449). A November 11, 1996 flight log entry, confirmed by grand jury testimony, places Schantz on an Epstein flight from Palm Beach to Teterboro alongside Epstein, family members, and a minor (EFTA00008920). These three records — legal negotiations, property fiduciary power, and travel in Epstein's inner circle — all predate his formal trust appointments by five years, establishing that Schantz was embedded in Epstein's operations from the outset of their relationship. The Martindale.com legal directory later listed his affiliation as "J. Epstein & Co., Inc." with practice areas spanning international law, corporate law, tax law, securities law, and litigation — the full spectrum of an in-house general counsel.

sections.title: Trust and Estate Architecture
sections.content:
The Hart Trust, dating to approximately 1998-1999, represents the earliest known trust instrument naming Schantz. It designated him as successor Trustee if no other trustee was acting: "If at any time no Trustee is acting and no successor has been designated or no successor who has been designated is available to act, JEFFREY A. SCHANTZ is appointed as successor Trustee" (EFTA01295536, EFTA01385730). This arrangement predated the more elaborate 2001 trust structure and demonstrates that Epstein had already vested fallback fiduciary authority in Schantz by the late 1990s.

The November 8, 2001 trust instruments elevated Schantz to the apex of Epstein's estate architecture. Trust One, established between Epstein as Grantor and both Epstein and Schantz as co-Trustees, directed all of Epstein's property into trust and designated a $10 million bequest to Schantz upon Epstein's death — the same amount designated for Mark Lawrence Epstein, Jeffrey's brother. Article XII granted Schantz singular authority to "designate one or more additional or successor Trustees" and to "remove any Trustee acting hereunder" (EFTA01266298). Indyke served as his backup: if Schantz resigned or could not act, these powers would pass to Indyke, not to Epstein himself. Epstein's original will named Schantz and Paul Hoffman as co-Executors, with Schantz authorized to designate and remove successor Executors (EFTA00016841). The concentration of appointment and removal power in a single non-family member is structurally unusual and suggests that Schantz, not Epstein, was intended to serve as the ultimate control mechanism for the estate in the event of Epstein's death or incapacitation.

Trust Two, executed the same day, named Schantz and Epstein as co-Trustees with identical appointment and removal powers vested in Schantz (EFTA01266334). Its sole beneficiary upon Epstein's death was Kelly Bovino at 100 percent. Bovino was later accused by Virginia Giuffre of sexual abuse, ignored a federal subpoena in the Maxwell case, and was identified as an Epstein procurer. The designation of a single alleged co-conspirator as the sole beneficiary of a trust administered by Schantz raises questions about the purpose of the vehicle and Schantz's awareness of its context. Both trusts were later restructured on January 27, 2012, replacing Schantz with Indyke, Andrew Farkas, and Jes Staley as co-Trustees — though Staley never executed either amended agreement. Both trusts were ultimately revoked in October 2012.

sections.title: Corporate and Banking Authority
sections.content:
Schantz simultaneously held multiple officer positions in Epstein's USVI corporate infrastructure. He served as Vice President, Secretary, and Treasurer of the J. Epstein Virgin Islands Foundation, Inc. — effectively holding three of the four standard officer positions, with Epstein as Treasurer in one filing and Paul Hoffman as VP in another (EFTA01377355, EFTA01298351). He was a founding Trustee of the Foundation alongside Hoffman and Epstein, operating from 6100 Red Hook Quarter, Suite B-3, American Yacht Harbor, St. Thomas, VI 00802. The Foundation articles organized the entity under USVI Nonprofit Corporations Law as a 501(c)(3) for charitable, educational, and scientific purposes, but the concentration of officer roles in a single individual undermined the governance independence that nonprofit status presumes.

Banking records confirm Schantz's authority extended to direct control of Epstein's financial accounts. He was authorized signatory on the FirstBank Puerto Rico commercial checking account for Epstein Virgin Islands Foundation Inc. T/A Enhanced Education, opened September 7, 2000, with the only other authorized signatory being Epstein himself (EFTA01273238). This was the only FirstBank account listing Schantz; all subsequent accounts (2001 onward) listed Indyke instead, documenting the transition period in real time. At Deutsche Bank Private Wealth Management, Schantz was authorized on the J. Epstein Virgin Islands Foundation brokerage account with powers to "deposit, deliver, assign, withdraw and transfer funds and securities" (EFTA01282376). A Deutsche Bank (Chase Manhattan) account opening document confirms his VP/Secretary designation across banking relationships, listing Epstein as President and Schantz as VP/Sec at the St. Thomas address (EFTA01268689).

sections.title: Operational Logistics and the Wexner Channel
sections.content:
More than 50 FedEx invoices spanning May 1999 through August 2004 document Schantz as a central logistics node for Epstein's business operations, sending packages from J. Epstein & Co. and later NYSG LLC at 457 Madison Avenue to destinations across the Epstein network (EFTA01313190, EFTA01319611). The shipping account itself transitioned from "J EPSTEIN & CO INC" in 1999 to "NYSG LLC" by 2001, both at the same 457 Madison Avenue address, tracking the broader corporate rebrand. Schantz shipped to Morgan Stanley Dean Witter in West Palm Beach, to Chris-Craft Industries in Boca Raton (controlled by Herbert Siegel), to Ranieri & Co. in Uniondale, New York (founded by mortgage-backed securities pioneer Lewis Ranieri), to Gary Kerney at Zorro Ranch in Stanley, New Mexico, to Marjorie Robert at Opal Rise Executive Office in the USVI, and to the IRS in Columbus, Ohio.

The Columbus, Ohio delivery channel is particularly significant. FedEx records show at least three separate NYSG-to-Wexner-orbit delivery routes: to Tim Lyons at TIC Limited WC (The Limited Inc. world headquarters) at Three Limited Parkway, Gahanna, Ohio; to Herb Wolman at 38 Jefferson Avenue, Columbus (an insurance office); and to "On Jaffe" at 2209 Frenleaf Lane, Columbus. Additional recipients included Steve Hutkai, Peg Ugland, Paul Burkhardt, Karl Koon (at Abigail House, New Albany), and Donna Larsen, all connected to Wexner's corporate ecosystem (EFTA01315419, EFTA01319611). Schantz also shipped tax correspondence to Karen Zimmerman at the IRS office at 200 N. High Street, Columbus, and to attorneys at Vorys Sater Seymour and Pease, a Columbus law firm — suggesting that the Columbus shipments encompassed both Wexner business operations and Wexner-related tax and legal matters (EFTA01313417). Separately, multiple shipments to Vicki Sweigart at Chris-Craft Industries, 5355 Town Center Road, Boca Raton, connected Schantz to the Epstein-Herbert Siegel financial relationship (EFTA01319164).

FedEx records also reveal Schantz's travel patterns on Epstein business. A March-April 2002 shipment addressed to "JEFFREY SCHANTZ C/O EL SAN JUAN HOTEL" was sent internationally by Jeffrey E. Epstein himself, consistent with Schantz's signatory role on FirstBank Puerto Rico accounts (EFTA01313406). An August 2002 shipment from Lauren Kwintner at NYSG was addressed to Schantz at The Ritz-Carlton, San Francisco (EFTA01317721). A November 2003 message intercepted by Ghislaine Maxwell's assistant Michelle confirmed that Schantz exercised managerial authority at NYSG: "I spoke to Lauren & she says that on Oct 21 Jeff Schantz approved her holiday request for Dec 22 - Jan 2" (EFTA02332644). This places Schantz in an operational management role over NYSG staff as late as October 2003.

sections.title: The FTC-Citibank Litigation
sections.content:
Schantz provided sworn declarations in Financial Trust Company v. Citibank (D.V.I. Civil No. 2002-108), a case that reveals the scope of his involvement in Epstein's investment activities. The dispute centered on a $10 million loan originated August 2, 1999, with an express condition that the funds be used exclusively for an AIG-managed venture capital investment. When FTC sought to replace AIG as fund manager, Schantz's declaration (paragraph 5) confirmed that "FTC's advisors" — including Schantz — contacted Citibank employees to coordinate the replacement (EFTA01386058). His declaration further detailed information-gathering from Citibank, Salomon Smith Barney, and Chase Manhattan trust officers about AIG fund investor identities (Schantz Declaration paragraphs 6-8). In August 2001, Schantz participated in a telephone conference where he learned SSB had an investment banking conflict with AIG that precluded them from serving as replacement manager.

The parallel New York action, Citibank NA v. Epstein (SDNY 1:02-cv-05332), filed July 11, 2002, alleged that Epstein defaulted on two separate $10 million promissory notes, totaling $20 million. The defense was handled by Gerald B. Lefcourt, the celebrated criminal defense attorney, alongside Marshall Howard Fishman. A February 2003 New York Post article by Paul Tharp — "HOTSHOT EPSTEIN NOT SO HOT: VF" — identified Schantz as "Epstein's lawyer" and noted that "Epstein and his lawyer, Jeffrey Schantz, couldn't be reached for comment" (EFTA02729242). This was the earliest public media identification of Schantz's role. The New York case was terminated July 26, 2005. Schantz's declarations in the USVI proceeding establish that his responsibilities extended beyond trust administration and corporate officer duties into active investment management and financial dispute resolution on behalf of Epstein entities.

sections.title: Departure and Systematic Removal
sections.content:
Schantz's severance from the Epstein network was executed through a methodical sequence of legal instruments during 2003-2004. The First Codicil to Epstein's will, dated June 2003, replaced Schantz and Paul Hoffman as Executors with Henry Jarecki and James Cayne (EFTA00016841). A contemporaneous trust amendment removed Schantz as co-Trustee of Trust One, replacing him with Ghislaine Maxwell and Ira Zicherman — he was the only person whose removal required two successors, underscoring the breadth of responsibilities he had held alone (EFTA01266298). The Second Amendment to Trust One, dated December 2004 and notarized by Lauren J. Kwintner, formally deleted the subparagraph providing the $10 million bequest to "JEFFREY A. SCHANTZ or if he is not then living to his then living issue" (EFTA01266322). The same amendment redirected $20 million to Trust Two, suggesting that Trust Two became the vehicle for assets that had been earmarked for Schantz-related distributions.

A $500,000 NYSG LLC disbursement to Schantz on October 17, 2003 (EFTA01514000) — alongside a $200,000 disbursement to Indyke on the same statement, both funded by a $1,000,000 Epstein transfer on October 16 — may represent a severance payment or final compensation. In December 2016, when Mark Epstein asked his brother whether Schantz still worked for him, Epstein responded: "Left 13 years ago" (placing the departure at approximately 2003) and added "No bad guy" (EFTA02666903). The characterization suggests an amicable separation rather than a termination for cause. After departure, Schantz formed Hewlett Bay Associates LLC (circa 2007) at 800 Westchester Avenue, Suite S414, Rye Brook, New York — the same address listed on his Martindale.com profile — and later relocated to Florida, where FEC records show him donating to both Republican and Democratic candidates from addresses in Delray Beach, Boca Raton, Bradenton, and Lakewood Ranch. He currently describes himself as retired.

sections.title: Prosecutorial Attention and Legal Invisibility
sections.content:
Despite departing approximately sixteen years before Epstein's July 2019 arrest, Schantz remained on the radar of federal prosecutors. An internal SDNY email dated August 17, 2019 — one week after Epstein's death — identified Schantz alongside Indyke as the persons who "would (or would potentially be able to) send money on his behalf" (EFTA00018951). The email referenced a Deutsche Bank index spreadsheet with 2,000 rows, AmEx records, and discussed Epstein associates who might "communicate with, or who would send money on his behalf." That prosecutors named a person who had left Epstein's employ in 2003 as a current financial risk in 2019 suggests either continuing undocumented involvement or prosecutors' recognition that Schantz's deep institutional knowledge of Epstein's financial architecture made him a persistent concern. After Epstein's death, both Indyke and Schantz hired criminal defense attorneys, according to the Yahoo Finance investigation.

A comprehensive search across federal databases yields an unusual negative pattern. CourtListener returns zero cases with Schantz as a named party. FARA shows zero registrations. The FOIA-derived investigations database has zero mentions. SEC EDGAR contains no filings referencing him. He has no state-level corporate registrations in his own name across all searched jurisdictions. A single federal lobbying registration for a "Jeff Schantz" with JGW International Ltd. in 2006-2007, lobbying for Protonex Technology Corporation on defense and homeland security matters, may reference a different individual given the post-Epstein timeframe and unrelated industry. Schantz's entry in Epstein's Black Book (page 79) lists six phone numbers, a dedicated NYSG email address (jas@nysgllc.com), and an American Airlines frequent flyer number — comprehensive contact infrastructure for a person who subsequently achieved near-total invisibility in public records. The contrast between the density of his documented role within Epstein's structure and his absence from all external databases is itself investigatively significant, consistent with someone who operated exclusively through Epstein entities and never built an independent professional identity that would generate its own paper trail.
